To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability and folding yield of the V(H)-V(H) domain pair is higher than that of V(H)-kappa or V(H)-lambda domain pair and that the V(lambda) domains have a higher stability in the scFvs than in the single domains.
the human V(H)3, V(kappa)1 and V(kappa)-3 domains have high intrinsic stability and that the human V(Lambda)1 domain has a strong tendency to form stable scFv fragments with any V(H) domain.
1) The isolated V(H3) and V(kappa3) domains are the best domains in terms of stability and expression yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most suitable antibody variable domains for the generation of stable antibody fragments.
the development of a new antibody technology, which is based on a library of antibody fragments with improved biophysical properties.
the biophysical properties and interactions of the individual domains and how these can be exploited in the design and construction of antibody fragments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biophysical properties are determined by the individual domains as well as by the interactions between the domains.
the biophysical properties and expression yields of the V(H) and/or V(L) germline consensus sequences of the HuCAL are sufficient for the construction of high-quality antibodies.
the biophysical properties and the stability of the V(L) domain is of greater importance than those of V(H) domains for the stability of scFvs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the V(H)3 domain has the most favorable biophysical properties of all V(H) domains.
the biophysical properties are not only determined by the framework sequence, but also by the CDR sequences.

the biophysical properties can be improved by a combination of the following strategies: 1) use of a V(H) domain with a high intrinsic stability, 2) use of a framework with a high intrinsic folding yield, 3) use of a combination of V(H) and light chain domains with a high affinity for each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of the V(H) and the V(L) domain can be tuned to some extent by changing the amino acid sequence in the framework regions.
there are no general rules for the design of stable and soluble antibody fragments.
the V(H) and the V(L) domains of an scFv fragment can be chosen independently of each other, which gives a high degree of freedom in the selection of the antibody fragment.
